title: Schema Drift Detection & Handling in Production

scenes.heading: Schema Drift
scenes.subheading: When the shape of data changes underneath you
scenes.narration: Schema drift happens when an upstream source silently changes the shape of its data, and detecting it early prevents broken pipelines downstream.

scenes.heading: How drift shows up
bullets: A column is renamed or dropped without notice
A field's type changes, such as int to string
scenes.narration: Drift often appears as a column being renamed or dropped without any warning from the source team. A field's type may change, breaking casts and joins downstream. New columns can appear that your pipeline never expected, and even a shift in nullability or allowed enum values can silently corrupt logic.

scenes.heading: Two ways to handle drift
scenes.narration: One strategy is to fail fast, halting the pipeline the moment the schema diverges to protect everything downstream, at the cost of needing a human to intervene. The other is to evolve, automatically absorbing backward-compatible changes so data keeps flowing. Evolution keeps things moving but risks letting a subtle breaking change slip through unnoticed.

scenes.heading: A schema contract check
scenes.narration: This check compares the incoming dataframe against an explicit expected contract of columns and types. It raises a clear drift error the moment a column disappears or its type no longer matches. Running this at the pipeline's entry point turns silent schema changes into loud, actionable failures.

scenes.text: Enforce a schema contract at ingestion, quarantine drifting records, and negotiate changes with upstream teams before they break you.
scenes.narration: Enforce an explicit schema contract at ingestion, quarantine records that drift, and negotiate schema changes with upstream teams before those changes reach production and break you.
